newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's WMC eyes growth as profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Australia's WMC eyes growth as profits rise.

text.p: Australian nickel, gold and alumina giant WMC Ltd on Thursday announced a 20.4 percent leap in annual profit, and vowed to continue its aggressive expansion by developing resource projects worldwide.
"Our objective is to maximise shareholder value by finding, acquiring, developing and operating mineral resource projects throughout the world," managing director Hugh Morgan said.
WMC reported net equity profit of A$386.2 million (US$305 million) for the year ended June 30. It declared an 11-cent final dividend, up from 12 cents, making 22 cents for the year, up from 20 cents.
Morgan told reporters in Melbourne that the result had been achieved through higher nickel and copper sales, and higher nickel and alumina prices.
Morgan predicted flat to higher output of WMC's key commodities in 1996/97 coupled with lower unit costs, but would not predict future profits.
WMC's capital expenditure budget for 1996/97 is about A$600 million, similar to 1994/95 but down on last year.
Its largest domestic growth commitment is the A$1.25 billion expansion of the Olympic Dam copper/gold/uranium/silver mine in South Australia.

"The momentum for that is now gathering pace. Real dollars won't be spent until early next year. Now it's a question of optimisation and the process of finalising the arrangements with plant contractors," Morgan said.
Expansion of the mine will lower costs and see its annual copper and uranium oxide production more than double to 200,000 tonnes and 3,700 tonnes respectively by 2001.
Other domestic growth opportunies include the St Ives gold mine expansion and 50 percent spare capacity in its Goldfields gas transmission pipeline, both in Western Australia, Morgan said.
WMC also has a range of growth opportunities in Uzbekistan, the Philippines and Cuba.

Negotiations continue with the Uzbekistan government over the development of the Zarmitan gold deposit, which is estimated to hold 24 million tonnes of auriferous ore containing 10 grams of gold per tonne.
"As we speak, the negotiations are continuing. We have the preferred tender (for the project) and we are...hopefully resolving the outstanding issues," Morgan said.
Drilling to evaluate the promising Tampakan copper prospect on Mindanao island in the Philippines was progressing, he said.

In Cuba, evaluation of the Pinares de Mayari West nickel deposit in partnership with state-owned Commercial Caribbean Nickel SA had started. Negotiation of government approvals and contract documentation was expected to be completed by the end of 1996.

Morgan reaffirmed that the Cuban assets were unlikely to be affected by the tough sanctions due to be imposed on Cuba by the United States under the Helms-Burton Act. "Our present advice is that we are not subject to that (act)," he said.
WMC also foresees expanded alumina production resulting from increased refinery capacity at its 40 percent-owned global alumina joint venture with Aluminum Co of America, Morgan said.
